title: Determination 2014/011: proposed alternative method for site subsoil class, Wellington
jurisdiction: New Zealand (MBIE determination under the Building Act 2004); comparative test only, not Alberta; NZ code references retained as written
code_edition: NZ Building Code as cited in determination; NZS 1170.5:2004 cited for subsoil classes; Code edition in force not stated on pages read

facts.text: Applicants (body corporate of a ten-storey apartment building, Victoria and Ghuznee Streets, Wellington) planned earthquake strengthening and proposed a new method for interpolating between site subsoil classes in NZS 1170.5:2004 as part of establishing Building Code compliance.
The authority advised it would not accept the method as a proposed alternative solution.
The building (about 1970) is founded on reinforced concrete piles; engineers' reports estimate bedrock about 50 m deep under alluvium, with the Wellington fault about 1.6 km northwest.
The 15 August 2013 application included a Seismic Subsoil Class Review (12 January 2011), a Desk Top Geotechnical Seismic Assessment (20 April 2012) and an April 2011 conference paper.
The conference paper proposed replacing spectral shape factors in NZS 1170.5 with site-effect terms continuous over site periods of 0.25 s to 1.5 s.
The authority's email of 21 June 2013 said the site response would need to be based on subsoil Class D unless a qualified geotechnical engineer justified a lesser class.
